title: PrintGuard plugin
description: The manifest of a PrintGuard plugin. See https://github.com/oliverbravery/PrintGuard/blob/main/docs/plugins.md

id.description: Identifies the plugin everywhere, 3 to 40 lowercase letters, digits or hyphens.

name.description: Shown on the panel and in Settings. Defaults to the id.

version.description: Your own version, shown beside the name.

description.description: One line about what it does.

permissions.description: What it asks for. The user accepts all of it or none of it before the plugin can be enabled.

anyOf.description: Monitor names, scores and alerts, camera and printer status.
Show a live feed in its panel.
Enable, disable and retune any monitor.
Add monitors, and delete them with their history.
Change any camera's picture and frame rate.
Add and delete cameras.
Take a still from any camera. With net, it can send your pictures anywhere.
Every monitor's score history and past alerts.
Add and delete printers. It can set credentials, not read them.
Change anything in Settings. It can set credentials, not read them.
Mint and revoke API tokens. It never sees the secret.
Pause, resume and cancel any print.
Show a message in the dashboard.
Play a sound on this device.
Send through your ntfy, Pushover, Telegram or Discord.
Reach the addresses it lists.
Reach this machine and the network around it.
Sign you in to a service. PrintGuard holds the tokens.
Put a picture behind the dashboard.
Answer other plugins on the channels it lists.
Call the plugins and channels it names.
Serve pages under /plugins/<id>/, reading your session cookie.
Approve or refuse every request to the hub. It can lock you out.

reasons.description: Why it wants each permission, in your own words, shown when the user is asked to accept them. One line per permission, and every one it asks for needs one.

secrets.description: Credentials you need but never see. PrintGuard draws a form for these, and you reference one as {{secret.name}} in a ctx.http request. Each line says what the user should paste in.

provides.description: Channels other plugins may ask you for, or hear you publish on. Needs the link:provide permission, and each line says what the channel answers.

consumes.description: The plugins and channels you call or listen to, each written plugin-id:channel. Needs the link:consume permission, and you reach nothing you do not name here.

oauth.description: Sign the user in to a service and hold the tokens for you. Needs the oauth permission, and the access token arrives as {{secret.oauth}}. No client id here: whoever installs the plugin registers their own app and PrintGuard asks them for it.

authorize_url.description: Where the user is sent to sign in.

token_url.description: Where the code is exchanged for tokens.

register_url.description: Where the user goes to register their own app, shown alongside the redirect URI to give it.

label.description: What the service is called, shown when the user is asked. Defaults to the authorize host.

surfaces.description: Where plugin.js draws. Defaults to a dashboard panel.

anyOf.description: A panel of its own on the dashboard.
Drawn on every monitor tile, once per monitor.
Drawn in every monitor's settings, once per monitor.

platforms.description: Where it runs. Leave it out for everywhere, and name a bare platform to cover its variants.

anyOf.description: Docker
NVIDIA image
Intel image
macOS
Windows
Browser

icon.description: An image in your plugin's folder shown beside its name in the catalogue and the installed list. Square reads best. Read from your repository at the pinned commit, or carried inside a zip install.

media.description: Screenshots or GIFs in your plugin's folder, shown as a gallery on your page. Read from your repository at the pinned commit, or carried inside a zip install.

assets.description: Files it ships beside its code, each named here and sitting next to plugin.js.

urls.description: The only addresses ctx.http and ctx.socket may reach, each a match pattern of scheme://host/path. Naming a private or loopback address needs the net:local permission as well as net.

events.description: The engine events that wake worker.js.

anyOf.description: Carries tag, status, body.
Carries camera_id, jpeg.
Carries from, channel, body, call_id.
Carries tag, from, channel, body.
Carries from, channel, body.
Carries monitor_id, now, buckets, alerts, stats.
Carries tag, state, text.
Carries monitor_id, camera_id, score, prediction, margin, ms, ts.
Carries monitor_id, score, action, ts.
Carries monitor_id, message, recovered.
Carries printer_id, status, progress, job.
Carries message.
The snapshot your permissions allow.

tick_s.description: Run worker.js this often as well, in seconds. 0, or 5 at the least.
